title: CHAPTER TWO. On the immortality of the soul, from the light of nature and the confession of barbarians, both ancient and recently discovered
pass_a_gloss: See our Alsted's Encyclopaedia, book 6, the pneumatic part 4, chapter 2. That our rational soul stands as free from destruction and survives after its departure from the body is shown by the light belonging toward nature and belonging toward Scripture, as toward two torches shining in the dark. CHAPTER TWO. On the immortality belonging toward the soul, from the light belonging toward nature and the confession belonging toward barbarians, both the ancient and those discovered in our own memory.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER TWO. On the immortality of the soul, from the light of nature and the confession of barbarians, both the ancient and those discovered in our own memory.

That our rational soul, free from destruction, survives after its departure from the body is shown by the light of nature and of Scripture, as by two torches shining in the dark. See our Alsted's Encyclopaedia, book 6, pneumatic part 4, chapter 2.
source_text: CAPUT SECUNDUM, De animae immortalitate, ex luce naturae & confessione barbarorum, tum veterum, tum patrum nostra memoria detectorum. Animam vero nostram rationalem ab interitu liberam post suum a corpore discessum superesse, luce naturae & scripturae, tanquam ad duas faculas in obscuro lucentes, ostenditur. Vide Alstedii nostri Encyclopaediae lib. 6, pneumatica parte 4. cap. 2.
